statement: One line holds a string s of lowercase letters. Print the number of distinct non-empty substrings of s. Insert every suffix of s into a trie, one character at a time, counting the nodes created: each new node is a prefix of a suffix that no earlier insertion spelled - which is exactly one distinct substring. The total nodes created is the answer, and the construction is the count.

example.why: a, b, ab, ba, aba, bab and abab - seven distinct substrings in all.

hint: Count node creations during insertion; no second pass over the trie is needed.
mistake: Counting all n(n+1)/2 substrings without deduplication - aaa has six substrings but only three distinct.
